title: Le avventure di Pinocchio
author: Carlo Collodi
blurb: A wooden puppet who lies, runs away and gets into every kind of trouble on his way to becoming a real boy.
note: Published in 1883 and the author died in 1890, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Enrico Mazzanti, Pinocchio, for the first edition of Le avventure di Pinocchio, 1883. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Il giornalino di Gian Burrasca (selezione)
author: Vamba
blurb: A nine-year-old boy gets a diary for his birthday and fills it with one disaster after another, most of them caused by trying to help. The first five weeks.
note: Published in installments in 1907 to 1908 and as a book in 1912; the author died in 1920, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Gaetano Chierici, The Mask, late 19th century. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: C’era una volta... Fiabe (selezione)
author: Luigi Capuana
blurb: Six fairy tales told the old way, with kings and queens, poor children, magic gifts and a werewolf, full of lively dialogue and repeated rhymes.
note: First published in 1882 and the author died in 1915, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The text is that of the 1902 seventh edition, revised by the author.
coverCredit: Enrico Mazzanti, Tizzoncino, for Spera di sole in Luigi Capuana’s C’era una volta..., 1902 edition. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Cuore: i racconti mensili (selezione)
author: Edmondo De Amicis
blurb: Five of the monthly stories a teacher gives his class: brave children in war and in peace, and a boy from Genoa who crosses the ocean alone to find his mother.
note: Published in 1886 and the author died in 1908, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The text is that of the 1889 Treves edition.
coverCredit: Raffaello Gambogi, The Emigrants (Gli emigranti), about 1894. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Rosso Malpelo
author: Giovanni Verga
blurb: A red-haired boy works in a Sicilian sand mine, where everyone treats him as bad luck.
note: Published in 1878 and the author died in 1922, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Antonio Mancini, The Street Boy (Lo scugnizzo), about 1880. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Il treno ha fischiato
author: Luigi Pirandello
blurb: A quiet clerk is carried to the hospital after he suddenly loses his mind, and his colleagues try to understand why.
note: Published in 1914, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Umberto Boccioni, States of Mind: The Farewells, 1911. Museum of Modern Art, New York. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Chiaroscuro (selezione)
author: Grazia Deledda
blurb: Five stories from the villages and sheepfolds of Sardinia, with shepherds, old men, a young wild boar and a doe, by the Nobel Prize winner Grazia Deledda.
note: Published in 1912 and the author died in 1936, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The text is that of a 1921 edition.
coverCredit: Antonio Ballero, March Morning (Mattino di marzo), 1903. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: La locandiera
author: Carlo Goldoni
blurb: Mirandolina runs an inn in Florence where her noble guests all court her, and she decides to make the one man who scorns women fall in love with her. A comedy.
note: First staged and published in 1753 by an author who died in 1793, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The text is that of the 1910 Venice edition of the complete works.
coverCredit: Pietro Longhi, The Faint, about 1744. National Gallery of Art, Washington. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Le tigri di Mompracem
author: Emilio Salgari
blurb: Sandokan, the pirate known as the Tiger of Malaysia, falls in love with the niece of an English lord. An adventure novel of jungles, sea fights and escapes.
note: Published as a book in 1900 and the author died in 1911, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Eugène Delacroix, Tiger and Snake, 1862. National Gallery of Art, Washington. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Il Principe
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
blurb: A short handbook on how a ruler wins power and keeps it, written in plain and direct Italian.
note: Written in 1513 and first printed in 1532 by an author who died in 1527, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Santi di Tito, Portrait of Niccolò Machiavelli, 16th century. Palazzo Vecchio, Florence. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: La Divina Commedia: Inferno
author: Dante Alighieri
blurb: Dante is led through the nine circles of hell by the poet Virgil. 34 cantos in verse.
note: Written in the early 1300s by an author who died in 1321, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Domenico di Michelino, Dante and the Three Kingdoms, 1465. Florence Cathedral. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Il fu Mattia Pascal
author: Luigi Pirandello
blurb: A man who is mistakenly declared dead decides to start a new life under a new name.
note: Published in 1904, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Edvard Munch, At the Roulette Table in Monte Carlo, 1892. Munch Museum, Oslo. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: I promessi sposi
author: Alessandro Manzoni
blurb: Two young lovers in 17th-century Lombardy are kept apart by a local tyrant, war and plague. A long novel.
note: Published in 1840 to 1842 by an author who died in 1873, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Francesco Hayez, The Kiss, 1859. Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
